plan_review.notes: Adversarial-style rubber-duck review of the stateless, marker-based, review-gated design. 4 blocking concerns: (1) no auto-trigger on review-issue close -> added issues:[closed,reopened] trigger + concurrency group; (2) any closed state treated as approval -> gated on state_reason==completed vs not_planned rejection; (3) no pin to reviewed file revision -> added epicContentHash + reviewHashMarker drift detection; (4) no concurrency control -> added concurrency group (group: epic-create). 3 non-blocking concerns addressed: node.id charset validation, description/review field type validation, duplicate epic_id across a multi-file batch (assertUniqueEpicIds). One non-blocking suggestion (CODEOWNERS entry for docs/knowledge/epics/**) consciously deferred as a separate governance change out of this tasks scope; noted in the PR/handoff. All fixes were refinements to the same core design (stateless marker-based issues, no control-plane file) rather than a different architecture, so plan_divergence=minor.

rounds.notes: Shell injection via workflow_dispatch epic_path interpolated into run: blocks; state_reason:null on a closed issue treated as approval; a stale not_planned rejection permanently blocking a revised (different-hash) plan.
Diagnostic promised a fresh review issue could be filed for a revised plan but no mechanism existed to create one; resolved by refactoring reviewMarker to embed the content hash directly.
fetchEpicIssues embedded a redundant per_page=100 query param; removed. Accepted low-severity concurrency-queue note.
Confirmation round: no remaining validated findings.

Reviewed the ensureLabelsExist fix (added after independent_grade round 1 found a blocker: GitHub silently drops unknown labels on issue creation, so a brand-new epic label would never attach and fetchEpicIssues label filter would never find the issue again, causing duplicate review issues every run). Confirmed correct placement (before fetchEpicIssues/any issue POST), correct 422-tolerance for cross-epic label races under the serialized concurrency group, and adequate test coverage. Clean.

findings.detail: ensureLabelsExist treats every 422 from create-label as an already-exists race. GitHub also returns 422 for validation failures such as invalid or too-long label names, so a bad epic_id/custom label can be silently ignored and the workflow then creates issues without the required label, reintroducing the duplicate-review/idempotency failure. Inspect the 422 error payload for an already_exists code/message or validate label names/length and rethrow other 422s.

independent_grade.notes: The workflow is otherwise narrowly scoped, well documented, and has strong coverage for review gating, idempotency, dependency ordering, and the intended label-creation ordering/race path. The main residual correctness/test gap is overbroad 422 handling for label creation; it is actionable but not blocker severity for the core happy path.
